title: Fragment-first hit
description: One record per line in fragment_hits.jsonl: a candidate found by querying a peptide's fragment ions when its precursor could not be found, because the precursor was modified by something nobody guessed. A modification shifts only the fragments containing the modified residue, so the rest of the ladder is mass-invariant to it and can be queried without naming the modification first. Matched fragments cite the ion_uids they came from, so a hit is traceable back to detections already in the ledger.

boundary.description: A modification on K or R blocks cleavage, so the peptide itself changes. Both boundaries must be queried or that class of modification is missed by construction.

matched.description: The fragments that were found. Each cites the detection it came from, so the hit is anchored in the ledger rather than asserted.

ion_uid.description: The detection in ions.jsonl this fragment is. Usually one that was unassigned.

missed.description: Queried fragments not found. Not merely a failure count: which ones are missing localizes the modification, since the shifted fragments are the ones containing the modified residue.

required.description: k. Demanding all n fails exactly when the modification is real, because some queried fragments contain the modified residue.

drift_offset_bins_applied.description: Fragments carry their precursor's drift with a systematic offset where mobility separation precedes fragmentation. Requiring the group to agree in drift as well as time is what keeps chance groupings down.

residue_range.description: e.g. "7-9", read from which fragments shifted.

precursor.description: Null when the precursor was not found. That is a result, not a failure: fragment-only evidence is still evidence and is reported as such.

delta_mass.description: Observed neutral mass minus the unmodified peptide's. Only computable when a precursor was found.

plausible.description: False when the peptide carries none of the residues the modification needs. A mass match on an impossible residue is not a candidate.

evidence.description: Kept separate from confidence.tier on purpose: this is a different kind of claim, not a rung on the identification ladder.

control.description: Non-negotiable. Fragment masses are not unique, so a hit means nothing without the same query run against sequences that cannot be there.

reversed_matched.description: Fragments matched for the reversed sequence, same scans, same drift window.

entrapment_matched.description: Same, for a peptide that cannot be in the sample (E. coli).

cohort_false_rate.description: Share of control queries reaching k across the run. This is the number that makes a hit publishable.
